title: Elvarika Backend: Auto Credit Refills, 30-Min Job Timeout | vitalii.no
description:
How a database migration gave Elvarika self-healing credits and a hard stop for runaway jobs — and closed three ways users could write data they should never have touched.

Behind Elvarika's redesigned frontend, credit top-ups had to be done by hand every month. A job stuck in the synthesis runner just sat there with no time limit, and there was no way for a user to cancel a job once it started.

A new PostgreSQL migration adds SECURITY DEFINER functions that return JSON matching the v2 frontend's contract, a monthly credit refill routine, and job-cancellation support. The Python runner gained a 30-minute watchdog that kills a job running too long, lock and statement timeouts to stop a stuck query from blocking others, and clip de-duplication before sending text to speech synthesis. The same migration closed three open write paths: users setting their own role or credit balance directly, the shared audio cache writable by any logged-in user, and profiles readable by anonymous requests.

Credits now refill automatically every month, a stuck job is killed after 30 minutes instead of running indefinitely, and three previously-open write paths into the database are closed.
